query: SELECT event_type,action,actor_login,created_at,updated_at,title,body,comment_id,comments,state,closed_at,file_time,repo_name,number FROM github_events WHERE repo_name='wireapp/wire-android' AND number=734 AND event_type IN ('IssuesEvent','IssueCommentEvent') ORDER BY created_at,file_time FORMAT JSON

data.title: Change to open source map service
data.body:
Wire is fantastic, finally, after a very long time of searching for a FOSS, encrypted chat service I've found one I can use and recommend. Thank you!

But I find it curious that a service where privacy and security is a key part, even to the point where you let us download the apk directly if we don't use Google Play Store (thank you for that!) still use Google Maps for your mapping feature. I don't want Google to know more about me/everyone than they already do, including places I'm interested in.

Please:

1. Let me use the map feature without Google Play Services
2. Change stop sending those who click on map links to Google Maps and switch to OpenStreetMaps or someone who uses data from OSM.

Thanks again!

data.title: Switch to open source map service
data.body: @forteller you are referring to the "share your location" view correct? It's not a webview,  the are using the Google Play Services maps class [https://github.com/wireapp/wire-android/blob/master/app/src/main/res/layout/fragment_location.xml], which makes replacing it exponentially more difficult and time consuming than just changing a url.

data.title: Switch to open source map service
data.body:
Yes, that's the feature I'm talking about. But if you receive one of those shared locations and you use Wire on desktop you are sent to maps.google.com in your browser. That's the link I'm talking about.

Also, just noticed: When clicking on it on Android, the Google Maps app opens up directly. I have it installed, unfortunately, but I'm not accepting the terms of service and won't use it. Instead we should be asked which mapps app we want to open the link in.

data.title: Switch to open source map service
data.body: Yes, exactly. I've updated the issue to try to make my intention clearer, and also added a third point for those receiving a map link on Android.

data.title: Switch to open source map service
data.body: The real issue here, IMO, is that instead of sending the location in a standardized neutral format that can be opened with whatever program you like, for instance OSMAnd on Android, it sends out links to the Google maps online service. The right way to do this would be to use the [GEO URI format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geo_URI_scheme). Another additional convenience format would be a provider-independent web link.
